title: A Bakery for the Songbook
premise: Marguerite Quintana has spent fifteen years keeping her late grandfather's lighthouse cottage, writing anonymous romance serials under a pen name, and quietly falling for Theo Marchetti, the baker whose lease on the ground-floor bakery is about to expire. When a letter her grandfather wrote eleven years ago—postmarked the week before his death—surfaces inside the bakery's walls during renovations, it reveals that he secretly left Marguerite the building itself, contingent on her claiming it publicly by name. Claiming the inheritance would expose her pen name, unravel the anonymity that protects her fragile new identity, and force her to choose between the career that saved her and Theo, who has loved both of her selves without knowing they were one. In the end, Marguerite signs for the deed at a town meeting, publishes under her real name with Theo's name beside hers in the acknowledgments, and reopens the bakery as theirs together.
about_author: Ada Zhou is the pen name of a former pastry cook who spent six years working dawn shifts in coastal New England bakeries before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who rebuild themselves one small, deliberate step at a time.

chapters.title: Flour at Dawn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Opening on her meticulous morning routine—lighthouse checks, then the bakery below where Theo slides her the first croissant of the day. Establishes fifteen years of small safe steps and her unspoken feelings. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by the fear that safety has become hiding.

chapters.title: The Serial Under a Pen Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We learn she writes a beloved anonymous romance serial; her editor pushes her to go public for a book deal, and she refuses. A scene where Theo reads her serial aloud to customers, unknowingly praising her words. Emotional beat: the ache of being celebrated while invisible.

chapters.title: Lease Runs Out in Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo receives notice that the bakery lease expires in ninety days; the landlord's estate is being settled and the building may be sold. He hides the letter from Marguerite to protect her. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Sorting her grandfather's lighthouse logs, she finds gaps in his final year and a reference to 'the arrangement' she never understood. Flashbacks to the accident fifteen years ago that made her retreat from public life. Emotional beat: grief reopening like a door left unlatched.

chapters.title: Renovations
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Preparing the bakery for a possible sale inspection, Theo's crew opens a wall and finds a tin box: an unopened letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to Marguerite in her grandfather's hand. Emotional beat: the past physically surfacing through plaster and lath.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Theo gives her the letter; she reads it alone at the top of the lighthouse. Her grandfather reveals he bought the building years ago and left it to her—but only if she claims it openly, by name, within a year of the letter's discovery. Emotional beat: shock curdling into anger at being tested from beyond the grave.

chapters.title: Why I Stopped Being Seen
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with flashback chapters in her grandfather's voice via the letter's enclosures. The full story of the scandal that drove her into anonymity—a plagiarized manuscript, a public humiliation—and how her grandfather's quiet purchase of the bakery was his way of anchoring her. Emotional beat: compassion replacing resentment.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Person
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers his favorite novelist's handwriting matches the notes Marguerite leaves on flour sacks. He says nothing, terrified of being wrong and more terrified of being right. Emotional beat: suspended recognition, love deepening through secrecy.

chapters.title: The Developer Arrives
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A developer offers cash for the building, pressuring the estate's lawyer to force a sale since no heir has claimed it. Marguerite realizes claiming the deed means a public hearing, her name in the paper, her pen name exposed. Emotional beat: the walls closing in from both directions.

chapters.title: Croissant Diplomacy
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marguerite and Theo spend a late night testing recipes for a festival, circling each other's secrets without landing. Almost-confessions interrupted twice. Emotional beat: intimacy built from shared labor and withheld truth.

chapters.title: Editor's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her editor delivers an ultimatum: reveal yourself or lose the book deal—the career that funded her recovery. Meanwhile the claim deadline and the sale hearing converge on the same week. Emotional beat: every door now requires walking through fire.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Log's Last Page
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She finds the final log entry her grandfather never filed: a plea that she stop measuring her life in safe steps, because 'a light that hides helps no one find harbor.' Emotional beat: permission granted by the dead.

chapters.title: Misunderstanding at the Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, believing Marguerite plans to sell and leave town (he misreads a lawyer's email), withdraws emotionally and accepts a job offer in another city. Marguerite reads his distance as rejection of her true self. Emotional beat: two people protecting each other straight into heartbreak.

chapters.title: Storm Watch
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. A coastal storm knocks out power; Marguerite runs the lighthouse manually while Theo shelters there. Forced honesty in the dark: she admits she's the novelist; he admits he's leaving. Neither says the other thing. Emotional beat: confession without resolution.

chapters.title: Empty Ovens
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Theo departs for a final interview trip; the bakery goes cold. Marguerite drafts her public statement claiming the deed and her name, then burns a draft in the sink out of fear. Emotional beat: rock bottom, the old pattern of retreat beckoning.

chapters.title: The Town That Read Her All Along
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Customers begin leaving annotated copies of her serial at the bakery door, having guessed after the storm-night slip. Instead of mockery: gratitude, recipes, stories of how her books carried them. Emotional beat: discovering visibility was never the danger she remembered.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the estate lawyer's office, she signs the claim papers—her real name, witnessed, notarized—then walks to the town hall to file them publicly just as the developer's agent arrives. Beat: the climax of the external plot; she chooses inheritance over invisibility.

chapters.title: Runway Lights
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the airport, about to board, Theo receives Marguerite's published open letter—her real name, her story, and a single line addressed to him: 'The lease was never the thing I was afraid of losing.' He turns around. Emotional beat: the romantic climax.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Theo returns at dawn; the reconciliation scene in the cold bakery, dough rising between them as they finally say everything plainly. They decide to contest nothing and share everything: the deed, the ovens, the byline. Emotional beat: warmth after long frost.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The formal claim hearing; the developer contests, but the grandfather's letter and the town's testimony carry the day. Marguerite speaks publicly for the first time in fifteen years, voice steady. Emotional beat: triumph earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Songbook
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Reopening day: the bakery renamed for her grandfather's songbook of sea shanties he sang while kneading. Her novel publishes with her real name; Theo's name appears in the acknowledgments first. Emotional beat: belonging made structural—name, place, person aligned.

chapters.title: First Light, Second Rise
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. One year later: morning routine transformed but still hers—lighthouse check, then down the stairs to a shared kitchen. She lights the lamp and starts the proofing dough, writing the opening line of her next book in her own name. Emotional beat: quiet, chosen, durable joy.
